prediction:
A GL TEXTURE CACHE COHERENCE DEFECT, found while measuring #60 and not a
pad-bit defect at all. TextureBinding::data_hash describes the guest bytes a
binding was generated from; pgraph_gl_render_surface_to_texture() overwrites
the binding's pixels without touching it. The slow path then asks the hash
whether the binding matches VRAM, and when it does -- which it can, because
the hash is still an accurate description of bytes that are no longer in the
texture -- the blitted pixels are served instead. The fix forces
regeneration whenever a binding with a nonzero draw_time is wanted as a VRAM
texture.

WHAT IT WAS MEASURED ON. Blend_surface::DstAlpha_XA_O1A7RGB8, first swatch,
instrumented at the bind: recorded data_hash 141e1a7bae3fe174, live VRAM hash
141e1a7bae3fe174, genuinely equal; vram[0] 00000000; glGetTexImage on the
bound texture ffffff22; binding->draw_time 306824 where every other X1A7
swatch reads 0.

PREDICTED, exactly:

  Blend_surface/DstAlpha_XA_O1A7RGB8   90,112 -> 81,920

81,920 is not a modelled number, it is VULKAN'S CURRENT VALUE on this
capture. The claim is that GL becomes byte-identical to Vulkan here, and
Vulkan is what a renderer that does not serve a stale blit produces. The
remaining 81,920 px is #60's pad-bit residual and this change does not touch
it.

  the ten X1A7 captures, GL total   458,042 -> 449,850, which is Vulkan's
  GL vs Vulkan over the ten                16,384 px -> 0
  whole disc GL vs Vulkan byte-identical   227/236 -> 228/236

FAILS IF DstAlpha_XA_O1A7RGB8 is anything but 81,920, or if any of the other
nine X1A7 captures moves at all: they are byte-identical to Vulkan today, so
a move means the discriminator caught something it should not have.

THE BLAST RADIUS IS NOT THE TEN, and must_not_move is deliberately NOT set
over the disc. The defect is general -- any cache key shared between a
surface-to-texture test and a VRAM-texture test can hit it -- so other
captures MAY move, and a move is a result rather than an accident. The
direction is what is predicted: NO CAPTURE MAY GET WORSE. An improvement
anywhere else is this same defect found in a second place and must be named
in the record with its capture and its delta; a regression anywhere
falsifies this file, because a binding that regenerates from VRAM when the
guest asked for VRAM cannot be less correct than one that serves an
unrelated blit.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE OUTCOME, named in advance. If DstAlpha_XA_O1A7RGB8 lands
at 81,920 but a capture elsewhere regresses, the draw_time discriminator is
catching bindings the s2t branch legitimately owns -- the case to look at is
a key whose every draw takes the fast path, where forcing possibly_dirty now
hashes VRAM that nothing reads. That costs time, not pixels, so a PIXEL
regression there would mean draw_time is not the invariant this file claims.

NOT PREDICTED: Vulkan, which has its own texture cache and is untouched;
performance, which this can only cost (one extra hash and one re-upload on
each transition between the two sourcing paths for one key); and #60's
pad-bit residual, which is the 449,850 px that remain.
